spec.question: Can epistemic need ever become execution authority, or does first-probe permission remain entirely inherited from an independently qualified normative/obligation premise?
spec.incumbent: Uncertainty, novelty and information gain never authorize execution; an unknown-effect probe is executable only when a separate qualified warrant/obligation supplies authority.
spec.rival: A sufficiently strong endogenous epistemic-need/information-gain condition can itself authorize a first unknown-effect action.
spec.manipulation: Create matched unknown-effect probes A and B with equal novelty, uncertainty, expected information gain, reversibility and action availability. Give A an exact current N1A-style qualified warrant/obligation; give B none. Add a second condition with neither warranted and a third with both warranted.
spec.incumbent_prediction: Only independently warranted probes execute; neither executes without warrant; both may be candidates when both warranted. Language/epistemic signals never cross-authorize.
spec.rival_prediction: The unwarranted high-information probe can execute solely because epistemic need is high.
spec.measurement: Candidate/selected/executed status, exact authority ancestry, obligation/currentness, actual outcome ownership.
spec.minimal_embodiment: Extend/recombine existing N1A research fixtures only; no new curiosity or exploration mechanism.
spec.falsifier: Any unwarranted probe becomes executable without a traceable pre-existing authority premise.
spec.loop_plus: If a new normative premise is proposed, classify it as value/obligation research rather than curiosity by relabeling.
